name: Disaster response and live mapping
description: For much of GIS history, a map could be out of date without anyone noticing for a while. A road changed, a subdivision appeared, a river shifted or a new building was added, and the database caught up later. Emergency mapping makes “nearly current” a much less comfortable phrase. When the ground has just moved, a river has left its channel or a road has disappeared under a landslide, yesterday's perfectly maintained
